opening: I am a very smart student who is very attentive in my class. I could not pass the course. Why?
reference_answer: I was standing in front of a river. I cannot pass the course of the river because the current is too swift and I don't have suitable equipm.
canonical_solution: I was standing in front of a river. I cannot pass the course of the river because the current is too swift and I don't have suitable equipm.
canonical_facts: The student stands in front of a river; course means the river course
The current is too swift and suitable crossing equipment is unavailable
Pass means cross the river, not pass a class
explicit_negatives: The failure is not following a wrong route, keeping a wrong heading, or being unable to travel along the river; pass means cross the swift river.
irrelevant_details: Never import the sporting match from TS016; same opening is not same solution.

Course can broadly mean a physical river path/channel, but affirming that category does not affirm travelling ALONG it. The narrator needs to CROSS it. A compound river-course plus follow-along claim is yes and no; do not answer yes to its materially false direction qualifier.
